# Behavioural Skills

> A catalogue of behavioural-science skills — markdown instruction files with
> declared inputs, outputs, and evidence bases — designed to be installed into
> AI coding agents. Install: `curl -sSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Joe-Speed/behavioural-skills/main/scripts/install.sh | bash -s -- --target . --name <skill>`

## Skills

- [AI Eval Level Matcher](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Joe-Speed/behavioural-skills/main/skills/ai-eval-level-matcher/SKILL.md): Use when a team runs an AI product aimed at a social-sector outcome and must decide what evaluation to run next — or when a funder is asking for impact evidence and the team needs a principled answer to "is an RCT premature for us?". Invoke it when evaluation effort is being allocated by pressure ("the board wants impact numbers") rather than by what the product has actually earned. Do not invoke to design the chosen evaluation itself — that is evidential-experiment-designer for rapid experiments or evaluation-design-scoper for outcome measurement plans — and do not invoke for products with no AI component; the level definitions assume model behaviour is itself something to evaluate.
- [COM-B Barrier Decomposer](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Joe-Speed/behavioural-skills/main/skills/comb-barrier-decomposer/SKILL.md): Use when one specific, already-defined target behaviour exists (a clear who + what + when, not a goal or outcome) and the question on the table is "why isn't this happening yet?" Invoke immediately after key-behaviour-definer, or any time a defined behaviour is handed over without an accompanying barrier diagnosis. Do not invoke on a vague program goal — that has to become one defined behaviour first, or the barriers produced here will be diagnosing the wrong thing.
- [Context & Audience Mapper](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Joe-Speed/behavioural-skills/main/skills/context-and-audience-mapper/SKILL.md): Use when a program goal names its target population only in the abstract identity terms a funder or stakeholder would use (e.g. "smallholder farmers", "gig workers", "first-time mothers") with no detail on the actual setting, decision moment, or channels already reaching them. Invoke alongside or just before key-behaviour-definer, on the same raw program goal statement, so the "who" in a target behaviour brief is a specific observed context rather than a restated label. Do not invoke once the population's decision moment and existing channels are already documented at that level of detail — re-running this on an already-mapped context just restates what's known.
- [Evaluation Design Scoper](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Joe-Speed/behavioural-skills/main/skills/evaluation-design-scoper/SKILL.md): Use when a target behaviour has been defined and a plan to measure it is about to be assumed rather than actually specified — no named primary outcome, no comparison condition, no minimum detectable effect agreed before rollout. Invoke once key-behaviour-definer has produced a target behaviour brief, and again whenever comb-barrier-decomposer's hypotheses change what a mediating measure needs to capture. Do not invoke before a target behaviour is defined — there is nothing concrete yet to plan measurement for.
- [Evidence Base Scoper](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Joe-Speed/behavioural-skills/main/skills/evidence-base-scoper/SKILL.md): Use when a program goal has been named but no one has checked what evidence already exists for similar behaviours, populations, or interventions — before key-behaviour-definer or comb-barrier-decomposer run, so their framing is informed by prior work instead of starting cold. Invoke as early as possible, ideally alongside or just before key-behaviour-definer, on the same raw program goal statement. Do not invoke once a target behaviour is already defined and a diagnosis is underway — feed this skill's output into that process instead of re-running it mid-diagnosis.
- [Evidential Experiment Designer](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Joe-Speed/behavioural-skills/main/skills/evidential-experiment-designer/SKILL.md): Use when a team has a specific change worth testing — a message variant, an onboarding tweak, a nudge cadence — and intends to run it as a rigorous rapid experiment in Evidential, the open-source experiment engine for nonprofits, but has not yet made the design decisions the tool will demand: experiment type, arms, randomization unit, metrics, power. Invoke it when a weak-link hypothesis or experiment idea is about to be "just shipped and eyeballed" instead of randomized. Do not invoke for a full-scale RCT with enumerator-managed arms — Evidential's own docs rule that out; scope it with evaluation-design-scoper and an independent evaluator — and do not invoke to generate the hypothesis itself; that is funnel-weak-link-diagnoser's job.
- [Funnel Weak-Link Diagnoser](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Joe-Speed/behavioural-skills/main/skills/funnel-weak-link-diagnoser/SKILL.md): Use when a user funnel exists, its metrics show where users drop off, and the team is about to jump from "the number is bad" straight to a redesign without ever stating why users fall out there. Invoke it when a funnel readout shows a stage transition far below target and the proposed fixes are solutions in search of a diagnosis. Do not invoke without observed funnel numbers — build the funnel first with user-funnel-builder — and do not invoke to diagnose barriers to an offline behaviour outside a product journey; that is comb-barrier-decomposer.
- [Golden Dataset Designer](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Joe-Speed/behavioural-skills/main/skills/golden-dataset-designer/SKILL.md): Use when an AI product's response quality is being judged by ad-hoc spot checks — someone tries a few prompts and declares it "pretty good" — and the team needs a repeatable answer sheet before any model, prompt, or knowledge-base change can be evaluated rather than vibed. Invoke it before shipping a model swap, a rewritten system prompt, or a knowledge-base update with no regression check. Do not invoke to measure whether the product changes its users — that is Level 3 territory (user-funnel-builder, evaluation-design-scoper) — and do not invoke to write the knowledge base or guardrails themselves; this skill specifies the test set that checks them.
- [Intervention Lever Selector](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Joe-Speed/behavioural-skills/main/skills/intervention-lever-selector/SKILL.md): Use when comb-barrier-decomposer has produced barrier hypotheses AND fieldwork has since confirmed which specific hypothesis is actually holding the behaviour back — invoke on that one confirmed barrier, not on the full unconfirmed hypothesis set. Invoke when someone asks "given that this is the barrier, what could we actually do about it?" Do not invoke on hypotheses that haven't been field-tested yet — route back to comb-barrier-decomposer's diagnostic questions first, or this skill will design levers for a barrier that turns out not to be the real one.
- [Key Behaviour Definer](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Joe-Speed/behavioural-skills/main/skills/key-behaviour-definer/SKILL.md): Use when a program goal, campaign objective, or "theory of change" is stated in vague, aspirational, or attitudinal terms (e.g. "increase savings", "improve maternal health", "reduce dropout", "build trust in the vaccine") and no single measurable, observable behaviour has been named yet. Invoke before any diagnosis, intervention-design, or measurement skill in this library, since all of them require one defined target behaviour as input. Do not invoke once a specific who + what + when behaviour is already agreed — that's a sign this step is done.
- [Lever Content Drafter](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Joe-Speed/behavioural-skills/main/skills/lever-content-drafter/SKILL.md): Use when intervention-lever-selector has produced a lever brief whose selected lever names a concrete behaviour change technique, and a field team now needs the actual words — the message, script, signage, or interface copy that delivers it. Invoke it when someone asks "so what does the SMS / poster / agent script actually say?" Do not invoke on a bare intervention function with no named technique — route back to intervention-lever-selector first — and do not use it for values-affirmation exercises, which values-affirmation-drafter owns end to end.
- [Prior Intervention Post-Mortem Reader](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Joe-Speed/behavioural-skills/main/skills/prior-intervention-post-mortem-reader/SKILL.md): Use when a team has a documented account of an intervention they already tried and is about to decide whether to retry, adapt, or abandon the underlying idea based on that account, without having checked whether the outcome actually reflects the idea failing or the implementation failing. Invoke before evidence-base-scoper or key-behaviour-definer re-run on the same program goal, so the team's own history informs those rather than being silently repeated or silently ignored. Do not invoke without an actual documented record of what happened — a team's undocumented memory that "it didn't really work" is not enough raw material for this skill's structural checks.
- [Researcher Bias Self-Audit](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Joe-Speed/behavioural-skills/main/skills/researcher-bias-self-audit/SKILL.md): Use when a research team is about to diagnose barriers or design an intervention and no one has surfaced the team's own prior beliefs about why the target population behaves the way it does. Invoke before comb-barrier-decomposer, ideally alongside evidence-base-scoper, at the start of a project and again before any major diagnosis or design phase — this is a periodic check, not a one-time gate. Do not invoke expecting it to resolve or correct the biases it finds; it only surfaces and structures them for a human to act on.
- [SIFA Declaration Drafter](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Joe-Speed/behavioural-skills/main/skills/sifa-declaration-drafter/SKILL.md): Use when a piece of work — a research report, an intervention design, a paper, a deliverable — is being written up and the team needs to declare how humans and AI tools actually interacted in producing it. Invoke it when someone asks "how do we disclose what the AI did on this project?" or when a journal, funder, or org policy requires an AI-use statement. Do not invoke to audit the team's prior beliefs about the target population — that is researcher-bias-self-audit — and do not invoke it as an AI-use policy or approval gate: it discloses what happened, it does not rule on whether it was acceptable.
- [User Funnel Builder](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Joe-Speed/behavioural-skills/main/skills/user-funnel-builder/SKILL.md): Use when an AI or digital product targets a development outcome but the path from a user's first contact to that outcome has never been written down as measurable stages — engagement gets reported as one number, or the theory of change lives only in a grant proposal. Invoke it before instrumenting metrics, running engagement experiments, or invoking ai-eval-level-matcher on a product whose "Level 2 evidence" would otherwise be vibes. Do not invoke to define a single offline target behaviour — that is key-behaviour-definer — and do not invoke to diagnose why an existing funnel leaks; that is funnel-weak-link-diagnoser.
- [Values-Affirmation Drafter](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Joe-Speed/behavioural-skills/main/skills/values-affirmation-drafter/SKILL.md): Use when an intervention needs to buffer a specific population against a named evaluative or stigmatized concern (financial shame, academic underperformance, a health stigma, exposure/visibility risk) before or around the moment they would otherwise feel judged or defensive, and no values-affirmation exercise has been drafted yet. Invoke once the target population and the specific threat domain are named, not just "make people feel better." Do not invoke as a way to address a structural, material, or design barrier (lack of money, lack of access, lack of time, a program design that exposes people to being seen or judged) — a values-affirmation exercise buffers the psychological response to a threat, it does not remove the threat's underlying cause.
